memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "But if the rash does spread in their skin after they have shown themselves to the priest to be pronounced clean, they must appear before the priest again. The priest is to examine that person, and if the rash has spread in the skin, he shall pronounce them unclean; it is a defiling skin disease." - Lev 13:7-8 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Here is a sobering turn. This person had already been declared clean. The matter was closed. And then it spread.

So back they go. A second examination. A different verdict.

The single most important diagnostic sign in this whole chapter is not colour or depth — it is spreading. Whatever stayed contained could be tolerated. Whatever grew had to be dealt with.

Sin behaves exactly like this, and we consistently underestimate it. We think of our compromises as static — a fixed amount of dishonesty, a manageable level of anger, a private habit that stays private. But nothing sinful in us stays the same size. Paul warned the Corinthians that a little yeast works through the whole batch of dough (1 Cor 5:6). James traces the line: desire conceives and gives birth to sin; and sin, when it is full-grown, gives birth to death (Jas 1:15).

Notice too that a past clean verdict did not settle the future. This person's earlier assessment was genuine, but it was not permanent protection. Which is why Paul writes: if you think you are standing firm, be careful that you don't fall (1 Cor 10:12).

The Christian life requires ongoing honesty, not a single moment of it.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What in your life is not staying the same size?
2. Have you assumed a past victory means you are permanently safe in that area?
3. Who could you invite to check on you in this area regularly?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, keep me honest about what is growing in me. Do not let me trust a past victory instead of present watchfulness, and give me grace to deal with things early. Amen.
